purpose: represent physical acoustic-treatment objects and their local boundary behavior without duplicating S3D geometry primitives
geometryRules: AcousticMate does not define a parallel primitive type system
the geometry of an AcousticObject is an instantiated S3D Primitive
the semantic acoustic object type and the S3D primitive type are independent
a bass trap may use Box, Cylinder or another suitable S3D primitive without changing its bass-trap acoustic identity
any S3D primitive supported by the renderer may be used
new reusable primitive implementations belong in S3D/core, not AcousticMate
physical acoustic-treatment objects have finite volume and thickness
Plane is not required as a physical AcousticObject primitive
Box and Cylinder are sufficient canonical primitives for the initial treatment-object library
specialized names such as AbsorberMesh, DiffuserMesh or BassTrapMesh must not duplicate existing primitive geometry

boundaryModels.open: energy leaves the solved room and exterior geometry is not solved
boundaryModels.absorptive: frequency-dependent energy loss described by an absorption/material profile
boundaryModels.scattering: frequency-dependent redistribution of reflected energy; exact scattering physics may require a later solver
boundaryModels.impedance: general frequency-dependent boundary impedance model reserved for solver strategies that support it

semanticObjects.absorber: AcousticObject using an S3D Primitive plus an absorptive boundary/material model
semanticObjects.diffuser: AcousticObject using an S3D Primitive plus a scattering boundary/material model
semanticObjects.bassTrap: AcousticObject using an S3D Primitive plus an absorptive or impedance model

boundaryPatch.purpose: apply a local boundary condition to a bounded area of an existing room surface
examples: surface area covered by an attached absorber
surface area influenced by an attached diffuser

openingRule: an opening remains a BoundaryPatch in the room surface and is not represented as a finite-volume AcousticObject
attachmentRules: an AcousticObject may exist free-standing or attached to a room surface
when attached, its wall-facing/contact relation may generate or bind a BoundaryPatch for solver use
RoomEditor presents AcousticObject placement as world-space X, Y and Z center coordinates rather than exposing wall, offset or sill-height as primary placement controls
wall, offset and sill-height may remain an internal solver-facing representation of a RoomSurfaceAttachment
editing world-space X, Y or Z for a wall-attached AcousticObject updates or resolves the corresponding surface attachment without silently detaching the object
gizmo position changes for a wall-attached AcousticObject follow the same world-space placement rule as numeric X, Y and Z editing
primitive rotation is presentation geometry unless a solver strategy explicitly declares orientation-dependent boundary physics
render geometry and acoustic boundary behavior are separate concerns
the solver must consume acoustic models/boundary patches rather than infer treatment physics from primitive names
solverRules: the current rectangular modal solver may approximate absorptive treatment as mode-dependent loss over affected boundary area
the current rectangular modal solver must not claim exact diffuser scattering behavior
exact mixed-boundary, impedance or scattering behavior may require numerical or reflection/scattering solver strategies
unsupported boundary physics must be explicit rather than silently treated as exact
applicationRules: RoomEditor may create, place, move, rotate, resize and remove AcousticObject instances
global transform gizmo enable applies to acoustic treatment objects as well as speaker objects
AcousticMate may provide reusable material/acoustic profiles without fabricating measured manufacturer data
AcousticMate must not automatically recommend absorber or diffuser placement unless a separate explicit feature contract later allows it
